summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis following Nissen fundoplication was admitted for a two-day episode of nausea, vomiting, and increased bowel movements triggered by a fizzy drink. She presented with metabolic acidosis, hypokalemia, and transient hypertension, all of which resolved with IV fluids, electrolyte repletion, and bowel rest. She was maintained NPO initially, treated with IV antiemetics, and enteral nutrition was restarted on hospital day 3. Her nausea improved, she tolerated a clear liquid diet, and was discharged home in stable condition. No infectious cause was found on stool or blood cultures. Discharge instructions included resuming home medications, advancing diet gradually, and follow-up with her primary care provider.
